close your eyes think : future what do you see

Emotions colour our impressions of the future. Images of what the world will be like in the years ahead are based on how we feel about those years. Fear, despair and uncertainty translate into pictures of unliveable cities, destroyed nature, conflict. Hope, trust and curiosity evoke images of new ways of life, world peace and interplanetary life. Dystopia, utopia – big, epic world views, mirrors of our inner world.

We have lively imaginations when it comes to those future worlds. But can we be as imaginative about ourselves? How do we humans see ourselves when we look forward in time? Who are we now, and who will we become? Change – how does it feel? Can we practise change? Can we practise for the future?

Inspired by the French cult novel La Horde du Contrevent (2004) by the sci-fi author Alain Damasio, the choreographer Lisi Estaras has created a dance production in which she leaves the world we know far behind. She has assembled a cast who are seldom seen in our theatres: an intergenerational group of dancers with and without disabilities. RAFAGA means a sudden, fierce gust of wind. An obstacle to our freedom of movement, a disruption of our balance. But it also heralds something new. Something whose exact form is still unknown. And might this new form be something that each of us already carries inside?

"We can feel it: some forces refuse to move forward, voices cling to a stand still.
352813BDFD4C1DAF1BF267C886FCA955:
‘The world doesn’t revolve around us. We’re the world. Here and now. You and me. Because if we’re the world, then we can change it too. Deal?’

In a world that sometimes feels as if it’s about to explode, a boy tries to make sense of everything that’s happening. Until he meets her. She looks at everything differently: headstrong, fearless and with a head full of ideas.

In Anders dromen we met de dromedarissen , Jan Sobrie ( Lenny , Titus , etc.) and Silke Thorrez ( Chantal , Nonkels , etc.) tell a playful and moving story about first love, big questions and the power of imagination. A performance full of hope for anyone beginning to discover how to dream up their own place in the world.
440D7749D98CE6F417216C6F5458BBC6:
Thomas is alone on stage. Nobody wants to play with him. He has no brother. He has no sister. He only has himself. So he fantasizes about trees, bears, ladies and gentlemen, birds without feathers learning a magic trick.

Ah, playing SOLO all on your own isn’t always fun. But what is it, then? That feeling of being lonely?

SOLO! is the new cabaret show for toddlers by the duo Thomas van Caeneghem and Lander Severins. You’ve seen them together before in BOTSKOP , Akke Akke Tuut and Stok Paard Prins (also in hetpaleis this year). This time, Thomas is alone on stage. Alone with his loneliness and his imagination. Luckily, he still has his guitar. And I think there’s also some sort of strange speaker ready.

690416CD8E987C3D9158B7B1C4326B0F:
Once, an old woman gave me a little boat in a bottle. That little boat had been stuck inside with glue. I say, ‘Thank you.’ And she says, ‘Never forget that sometimes there’s a sea inside an empty bottle.’ In Zwerflicht , the Fratelli seek a way out when innocence has vanished. Innocence that fades along with the light in the eyes. Because sometimes things happen that you, as a young person, have no control over, and what do you do then? How can you still see, in a dark room? How do you fix a crack in the head or glue back a body that’s broken?

Artistic director of Tutti Fratelli and actor Nico Sturm and theatre-maker, writer and performer Mokhallad Rasem are the ideal guides on this wondrous journey through hidden beauty.
87253ADC5B3685489D9CC28FFD3DA7E9:
Every first Sunday of the month, we make sure hetpaleis is extra cosy.

Six well-known and lesser-known artists read aloud from their favourite children’s book. This is followed by a (craft) workshop based on the story that’s just been read.

PS: coming and going is no problem, and you don’t have to sit still either.

B951ACD86567BE2888A9B52DA2DA5F70:
Sooner or later, the monster of the night pays a visit to everyone. It’s a strange visit: something whispers in your ear, and yet you feel completely alone. The monster of the night has many names. Some call it “fear,” or even “death,” while others call it “stress” or simply “change.”

Sometimes the monster of the night stands by your bed, silent as a mouse. But very often, it just can’t stop talking. And when the sun rises, it’s gone again.

With NACHT (NIGHT) , Jonas Baeke and Mats Vandroogenbroeck have created an intimate performance about fear. They portray a character who is overcome by a sense of dread at night. But what happens if we say “hello” to the monster? If we don’t try to chase it away, but talk to it instead? Are we still alone then? Are we still afraid?

NACHT (NIGHT) is the third collaboration between Mats and Jonas in the field of youth theater. Their previous performances, “Bambiraptor” and “Infinity Forever,” were both selected for the TheaterFestival. For this new performance, they expand their richly visual universe and enter the world of puppet theater.
